newsitem.title: UK: Tight NWE diesel market draws cargoes from Med.
newsitem.headline: Tight NWE diesel market draws cargoes from Med.

text.p: NWE heating oil premiums sagged on Tuesday, but a tight diesel market was starting to attract material from the Mediterranean, traders said.
An EN590 cargo was sold out of Italy on Tuesday to a Nordic refiner at fob high quotes +$1.50-$2.00 a tonne.
Other north European buyers also had uncovered requirements, Med refiners said.
"The arbitrage is open and functioning," said one.
Premiums for diesel cargoes in NWE were pegged at around June IPE +$10-$12, while June EN590 swaps were traded at +$10 and +$9.50 a tonne.
But lacklustre buying interest from German end-users weighed on the NWE heating oil market and barge premiums eased lower.
Barges traded at June IPE +$2.50 and $2.25 fob ARA, while material for early June delivery was talked at June IPE +75 cents/$1.50.
Diesel barges were talked at June +$9.50/$10.50.
